purpose: Scope the offline cosmetic-photo prototype; these sources do not validate its algorithms or thresholds.

sources.title: Courage + Khazaka scientific measurement instruments
observations: The manufacturer distinguishes hydration measurement with a Corneometer, gloss measurement, sebum measurement, and melanin/erythema reflectance measurement.
MoistureMap uses capacitance imaging; a conventional RGB photo is not that sensor.

sources.title: Canfield Scientific VISIA-CR
observations: Specialized facial analysis uses controlled lighting modalities and standardized capture.
The system distinguishes spot contrast, texture, dark circular pore appearance, wrinkles, and specialized UV or polarized observations.

implementation_scope: Heuristic image features within central cheek samples only; this is not a validated biological pore, pigment, or wrinkle detector.
Compact dark texture and line-like contrast may come from facial hair, shadows, makeup, filters, or compression.
Any feature width is in the analyzed image pixels; there is no physical scale calibration or millimeter pore size.
Visible color variation does not determine melanin concentration, a pigment disorder, or a diagnosis.
Moisture appearance is a best-effort visible-finish estimate from reflection cues, not actual water content or a hydration percentage. User-reported skin feel remains independent.

Resolution, focus, pose, lighting and noise qualify readable-image estimates instead of routinely withholding them. Invalid or unreadable pixels still cannot produce an estimate. A subtle signal does not prove absence of pores, pigment, or wrinkles.
No skin-health score, calibrated confidence, age estimate, treatment claim, automatic active-ingredient choice, or persistent photo/measurement storage.
